text: Where does alcohol go after you drink it?
The rest moves on to your small intestine.
Its large surface area absorbs alcohol faster.
From the gut, blood carries it to your liver first, through the portal vein.
Then it spreads through the water in your body, including your brain.
On an empty stomach, blood alcohol typically peaks in about an hour.
Meanwhile, your liver does most of the work.
An enzyme called A D H turns alcohol into acetaldehyde.
Then A L D H turns that into acetate.
More than ninety percent of the alcohol is broken down by your liver.
A small amount, about two to five percent, leaves unchanged.
That's in your breath, urine, and sweat.
